description: Benchmark for Day 06. Written and split (dev/test by topic) BEFORE any retrieval run. Evidence quotes are verified against the normalized corpus by starter/scripts/verify_benchmark.py, which also fills gold_page and enumerates every other valid page (accepted_gold) that contains the same evidence.
split_rule: Split by pydoc topic: dev uses try/raise/assert/for/while/booleans/global/augassign/assignment-expressions/lambda/strings/debugger/import; test uses match/typesmapping/class/with. Leakage risk: topic 'compound' repeats try/for/while/with/match/class text, so a test answer can also be found in 'compound' (accepted as alternative gold, documented).
filter_rule: filter is user context given BEFORE retrieval (the user states their Python version). It is never derived from the gold source. Strategy C applies it only when filter is not null; A and B ignore it.

questions.question: What happens to a pending exception if the finally clause executes a return statement?
questions.expected_answer: The saved exception is discarded.
questions.evidence_quote: If the "finally" clause executes a "return", "break" or "continue" statement, the saved exception is discarded

questions.question: Why can't I use the exception variable from 'except E as N' after the handler block ends?
questions.expected_answer: The name bound with 'as target' is cleared (deleted) at the end of the except clause.
questions.evidence_quote: When an exception has been assigned using "as target", it is cleared at the end of the "except" clause.

questions.question: Can one try statement contain both except and except* clauses?
questions.expected_answer: No; a try statement can have either except or except* clauses, but not both.
questions.evidence_quote: A "try" statement can have either "except" or "except*" clauses, but not both.

questions.question: What does a bare raise statement do when no exception is currently being handled?
questions.expected_answer: It raises RuntimeError indicating that this is an error.
questions.evidence_quote: If there isn’t currently an active exception, a "RuntimeError" exception is raised indicating that this is an error.

questions.question: How do I stop Python from showing the original exception as the cause when I raise a new one?
questions.expected_answer: Use 'raise ... from None' to suppress exception chaining.
questions.evidence_quote: Exception chaining can be explicitly suppressed by specifying "None" in the "from" clause

questions.question: Are assert statements still executed when Python runs with optimization (-O)?
questions.expected_answer: No; the code generator emits no code for assert when optimization is requested.
questions.evidence_quote: The current code generator emits no code for an "assert" statement when optimization is requested at compile time.

questions.question: If a loop is terminated with break, is its else clause executed?
questions.expected_answer: No; break terminates the loop without executing the else clause's suite.
questions.evidence_quote: A "break" statement executed in the first suite terminates the loop without executing the "else" clause’s suite.

questions.question: Do the and/or operators always return True or False?
questions.expected_answer: No; they return the last evaluated argument, not necessarily a bool.
questions.evidence_quote: Note that neither "and" nor "or" restrict the value and type they return to "False" and "True", but rather return the last evaluated argument.

questions.question: What error occurs if a variable is used in a function before its global declaration?
questions.expected_answer: A SyntaxError is raised.
questions.evidence_quote: A "SyntaxError" is raised if a variable is used or assigned to prior to its global declaration in the scope.

questions.question: In an augmented assignment such as a[i] += f(x), which side is evaluated first?
questions.expected_answer: The left-hand side is evaluated before the right-hand side.
questions.evidence_quote: Unlike normal assignments, augmented assignments evaluate the left- hand side *before* evaluating the right-hand side.

questions.question: When must a walrus := expression be wrapped in parentheses?
questions.expected_answer: When used as an expression statement and as a sub-expression in slicing, conditional, lambda, keyword-argument and comprehension-if expressions (and in assert, with and assignment statements).
questions.evidence_quote: Assignment expressions must be surrounded by parentheses when used as expression statements and when used as sub-expressions in slicing, conditional, lambda, keyword-argument, and comprehension-if expressions

questions.question: Can a lambda function contain statements or annotations?
questions.expected_answer: No; functions created with lambda expressions cannot contain statements or annotations.
questions.evidence_quote: Note that functions created with lambda expressions cannot contain statements or annotations.

questions.question: I am on Python 3.11. What warning does an unrecognized escape sequence in a string literal produce?
questions.expected_answer: A DeprecationWarning (the docs say it will become a SyntaxWarning and eventually a SyntaxError in the future).
questions.evidence_quote: Changed in version 3.6: Unrecognized escape sequences produce a "DeprecationWarning".

questions.question: Using Python 3.13, can pdb.post_mortem() be given an exception object rather than a traceback?
questions.expected_answer: Yes; post_mortem enters post-mortem debugging of the given exception or traceback object (exception support added in 3.13).
questions.evidence_quote: Enter post-mortem debugging of the given exception or traceback object.

questions.question: For Python 3.13, what normalization form must non-ASCII names listed in __all__ use?
questions.expected_answer: NFKC.
questions.evidence_quote: Names containing non-ASCII characters must be in the normalization form NFKC.

questions.question: Can I still use a variable captured by a successful case pattern after the match statement finishes?
questions.expected_answer: Yes; name bindings made during a successful pattern match outlive the executed block.
questions.evidence_quote: bindings made during a successful pattern match outlive the executed block and can be used after the match statement

questions.question: What happens if a mapping pattern contains duplicate keys?
questions.expected_answer: Duplicate literal keys raise SyntaxError; two keys that otherwise have the same value raise ValueError at runtime.
questions.evidence_quote: Duplicate literal keys will raise a "SyntaxError". Two keys that otherwise have the same value will raise a "ValueError" at runtime.

questions.question: Does assigning a new value to an existing dictionary key change the iteration order?
questions.expected_answer: No; dictionaries preserve insertion order and updating a key does not affect the order.
questions.evidence_quote: Dictionaries preserve insertion order. Note that updating a key does not affect the order.

questions.question: On Python 3.11, how does the documented equivalent code of a with statement look up and call __enter__?
questions.expected_answer: enter = type(manager).__enter__ and then value = enter(manager) (lookup on the type, manager passed explicitly).
questions.evidence_quote: enter = type(manager).__enter__ exit = type(manager).__exit__ value = enter(manager)

questions.question: In Python 3.13, how can the type parameters of a generic class be retrieved at runtime?
questions.expected_answer: From the class's __type_params__ attribute.
questions.evidence_quote: At runtime, the type parameters can be retrieved from the class’s "__type_params__" attribute.
